params.p: [1:tc Particular] Use a wide Box emitter so the soft particle volume spans the composition.
[1:tc Particular] Make the emission volume broad enough to avoid a localized cloud with visible boundaries.
[1:tc Particular] Build a dense but still diffuse atmospheric field.
[1:tc Particular] Keep particle travel slow for a drifting nebula rather than a particle burst.
[1:tc Particular] Emit uniformly in all directions for amorphous cloud structure.
[1:tc Particular] Keep particles alive long enough for a continuous fog-like volume.
[1:tc Particular] Use Glow Sphere particles to merge into soft cloud masses.
[1:tc Particular] Use oversized soft particles so individual dots fuse into nebula forms.
[1:tc Particular] Vary particle sizes to prevent regular-looking blobs.
[1:tc Particular] Keep each particle dim so the overall result remains a dark background-grade violet.
[1:tc Particular] Introduce restrained opacity variation for organic mottling.
[1:tc Particular] Set Color to At Birth before assigning the violet particle color.
[1:tc Particular] Color the luminous fog a deep violet rather than bright white.
[1:tc Particular] Additively blend the dim glow spheres into soft nebula density.
[1:tc Particular] Enable air resistance before turbulence so turbulent motion affects the cloud.
[1:tc Particular] Gently displace particles with turbulence to morph the cloud structure over time.
[1:tc Particular] Use large turbulence features for broad gaseous curls instead of fine jitter.
[1:tc Particular] Add enough turbulence detail for layered cloud variation.
[1:tc Particular] Enable modest motion blur to keep moving cloud particles smooth.
[1:tc Particular] Use a natural shutter angle that does not smear the soft texture excessively.
[1:tc Particular] Slowly drift the emitting cloud mass across the frame so t1 and t4 visibly evolve. (expr)
[2:BCC_TEXTURES] Add only a restrained surface grain so the cloud remains soft and dominant.
[2:BCC_TEXTURES] Increase fine texture detail for subtle close-inspection particle character.
[2:BCC_TEXTURES] Use a tight texture scale so the texture reads as grain rather than paper.
[2:BCC_TEXTURES] Keep the grain scale even in both dimensions.
[2:BCC_TEXTURES] Choose a non-default texture variation to avoid a generic repeating pattern.
